text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency SLO breach detected for smart-routing policy in us-east-1 (p95=1.35s, SLO=800ms) — automatic reroute attempts triggered 6x in last 10m. Paging @oncall-alex :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: on it. seeing big p95 spike on the routing metric dashboard. logs show a flurry of reroute decisions back and forth between us-east and eu-west for several tenants.

samir.r: i can pull the routing decision log. initial suspicion: policy hysteresis too low + fallback to eu-west which has higher tail latency under current load, causing oscillation.

jen.kaplan: any customer impact? do we have error increases or just latency regressions?

maria.perez: CS reporting increased timeouts on a few enterprise customers — CS ticket #5234 opened. they say frontend saw slow completions and some 504s.

oncall-alex: metric snapshot: overall error rate up from 0.05% -> 0.85% for affected routes, request volume steady. p99 also bumped to ~2.4s for those routes.

sre-lead: prioritize mitigation to stop the reroute loop first. Keep original model variants pinned while we investigate.

product-ops: if we pin, will throughput suffer? some customers rely on eu-west for capacity.

samir.r: short plan: 1) disable smart-region-fallback policy for the affected routing group (temp) 2) pin affected routes to model-variant v2-stable 3) raise routing-hysteresis to 60s to avoid flip-flop 4) monitor for 15m

oncall-alex: executing step 1 now: 
```bash
# disable fallback policy for routing-group 'svc-chat'
redwoodctl routing-policy update svc-chat --fallback-enabled=false --token $REDWOOD_OPS_TOKEN
```

oncall-alex: policy disabled. sending confirmation.

incident-bot: SYSTEM: Change applied by oncall-alex at 2150004368 

samir.r: pinning traffic to v2-stable for the affected routes now (canary off)

jen.kaplan: command?

samir.r: 
```bash
redwoodctl route set-variant --route svc-chat/* --variant v2-stable --duration 30m
```

samir.r: done. confirmed via routing logs, no more cross-region handoffs for those keys.

maria.perez: CS updated customers in ticket #5234: "we're mitigating an intermittent latency issue; recovery actions applied. will update when stable."

product-ops: ok keep an eye on throughput to eu-west for spillover.

oncall-alex: metrics 5m after mitigation: p95 down to 820ms (from 1.35s) for pinned routes, overall error rate back to 0.12%. still slightly above target but trending down.

sre-lead: we should also increase the routing-policy hysteresis threshold in config to avoid future oscillations. samir, can you propose a safe value?

samir.r: propose 60s hysteresis + require at least 2 consecutive SLO violations before triggering reroute. currently it's 10s + single violation. I'll test locally and then push.

jen.kaplan: after we stabilize, let's create a short-runbook for oncall to follow when smart routing flips like this.

product-ops: agree — also need guardrails in console so users can't set hysteresis too low.

incident-bot: NOTIFICATION: oncall handoff in 40m to night-shift. Please include mitigation summary in the handoff note.

maria.perez: CS: noting impacted customers list and sending account-level message template to affected teams.

oncall-alex: creating incident ticket and postmortem stub: INC-2026-1187. assigning to samir.r for root-cause + to jen.kaplan for runbook.

samir.r: initial root-cause hypothesis: routing decision logic misinterpreted transient remote tail latency as persistent, due to too-agile failover thresholds plus an under-provisioned eu-west model-variant that had higher p99 under burst. combination created a feedback loop where requests were sent to eu-west, raising its latency, then routed back, etc.

jen.kaplan: what about autoscaling? did capacity cover it?

samir.r: autoscaler reacted but by the time new replicas came up the policy had already bounced routes a few times. need better warm-up + avoid routing changes until scaling settles.

oncall-alex: timeline note for handoff: actions taken: disabled fallback policy (2150004368), pinned to v2-stable (2150004389), increased monitoring alerts, CS notified. current status: stable-ish, p95 ~780-850ms.

product-ops: severity assessment: P2 (multiple customers affected, partial degradations, mitigated).

maria.perez: CS notes saved in ticket; will send follow-up once RC confirmed.

incident-bot: REMINDER: include log snippets, routing-decision trace, and metric charts in postmortem.

oncall-alex: calling it stable for now. leaving a TODO to revert pins only after traffic normalizes for 30m and after hysteresis change deployed. handing to night oncall. @sre-lead, please accept handoff.

sre-lead: acknowledged, taking over. will coordinate the final rollback steps and ensure we have a clear rollback plan before unpinning.

cs-amy: Customer comms: sending status update in 10m.

jen.kaplan: created runbook PR: /docs/runbooks/routing-oscillation.md and assigned reviewers.

samir.r: follow-ups: 1) change policy defaults (hysteresis 60s + 2-violations) 2) add cooldown on reroutes during autoscaler events 3) postmortem with RCA + mitigation.

oncall-alex: closing thread to async follow-ups. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
